source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Taking the place of any other symptom management measures the client would otherwise still be receiving","B":"Being intended to intentionally hasten the client's death rather than to relieve their suffering","C":"Being applied routinely to essentially every client nearing the end of life, regardless of their specific symptoms","D":"Relieve otherwise intractable suffering by reducing consciousness, distinct in intent from euthanasia or assisted death"}}
source_row.rationale: Palliative sedation is intended to relieve otherwise intractable suffering at the end of life by reducing consciousness when other measures have failed, with the clinical intent being symptom relief rather than hastening death, distinguishing it ethically and clinically from euthanasia or assisted death; it is reserved for specific, severe circumstances rather than routine use.
source_row.source_detail: Intent and Appropriate Use of Palliative Sedation
